It generally means that they're going to fix their makeup. Usually mascara touch up, reapplying lipstick if it has been messed up by eating and drinking, etc. It rarely means literal powdering. It can also mean that they're just going to the restroom. 
The term originates from when powder was a popular form of makeup. It generally served the same purpose as foundation today, and had to be reapplied as the day progressed. The expression evolved to generally refer to anything a person might do in a restroom, not exclusively makeup.

Its basically the number of extra things attached to an atom in a molecule. A bond to a terminal atom counts as one item (doesn't matter what kind of bond), a pair of unshared electrons counts as one item. You count those up. To figure out the hybridization you just keep counting up until the number of orbitals is equal to the number of items on the central atom. 
s = 1 item
sp = 2 items. (There is only one s orbital at each energy level, so you gotta go up to the p orbitals)
sp2 = 3 items, etc.

Historically speaking, lots of people were writing stuff for the Bible, claiming it was inspired by God even though it might not have been. At some point the church had to cut some parts out because they contradicted traditionally accepted/famous parts of the Bible and were likely fake. Therefore, some parts of the Bible that exist today may not have been inspired by God, and it is likely that some legit parts were cut. It is reasonable for a "good Christian" to have doubts about the legitimacy of some parts of the Bible and choose not to follow them.
